technical: The evidence check failed. The headline measurement hpa_target_type came back with no value, so the claim 'KEDA 2.21.0 created an HPA target type of Value' has no verified measurement behind it. Fix: Change the HERO_MEASURE output in reproduce.sh and fix.sh so the scanner reads hpa_target_type for both configs, then rerun. Until then, quote the raw `kubectl get hpa -o jsonpath` lines with their log line numbers in the post.

technical: The 'verified workaround' changed two settings at once: scalingModifiers and a new HPA name. The 5-replica result can't be credited to scalingModifiers alone. The same-name run, described as reaching 5 at t=293s with FailedGetExternalMetric, isn't in the shown evidence. Fix: Add a control run with the fresh HPA name but no scalingModifiers. It should still show Value and 10 replicas, which credits the fix to scalingModifiers. Publish the same-name run's log with line numbers, or drop the caveat's numbers.

technical: The scale-up timeline is unexplained and doesn't match the stated arithmetic. With Value, the HPA should compute ceil(1×10/2)=5, but the log shows 4 at 48s and 8 at 107s. At t=166s the HPA wanted 8 while the Deployment had 10. The issue reports reaching max in under a minute, and the post never says why this lab took 166s. Fix: Capture the HPA's events and conditions (`kubectl describe hpa`, ScalingLimited) inside the window. Then explain the pace with HPA scale-up policy, KEDA pollingInterval and the 30s query duration (the issue used 10s), or say plainly that it is unexplained. Don't let readers treat 166s as typical.

editorial: The brief promised readers a way to check their own HPA. The lab ships check-affected.sh, but the post never mentions it or any by-hand check. Fix: Add a short 'Is your cluster affected?' section with `kubectl get hpa keda-hpa-<name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.spec.metrics[*].external.target}'`, `bash check-affected.sh`, and the AFFECTED/OK output from the run.

editorial: The post doesn't answer the reader's decision about the fix. It links PR 8327 but doesn't say what it changes (omitted metricType stays Value, explicit AverageValue is honoured, Utilization is rejected). It also doesn't say when scalingModifiers becomes removable, or that removing it renames the metric back. Fix: Add a paragraph: after upgrading to a release that contains PR 8327, keep metricType: AverageValue on the trigger and remove scalingModifiers. Expect the HPA metric name to change back from composite-metric. Say that if metricType is omitted, you still get Value.

editorial: The repro section asks readers to write their own Terraform provider and variables file before init. That is friction for something that should be one command. Fix: Commit providers.tf and variables.tf (region, lab_name, permissions_boundary with defaults) to the lab, and remove the sentence. Also rename SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN to SPLUNK_INGEST_TOKEN, since that is what it is.
outside claim without a known source: An upstream fix exists in KEDA PR 8327 with a matching docs PR 1921

claims.text: The Splunk Observability scaler builds the HPA metric target with v2.ValueMetricType instead of reading the trigger's metricType
The parser does not read config.MetricType for this scaler
The HPA controller keeps scale recommendations per HPA name for 300 seconds, so same-name migrations can stay high
Value is right for a fleet-wide aggregate that falls as pods are added, or a metric that is already per-pod
If you change the HPA name in production, dashboards and alerts need checking because the metric becomes composite-metric
An upstream fix exists in KEDA PR 8327 with a matching docs PR 1921
The Splunk Observability scaler docs list trigger parameters

brief.reader: Platform engineer autoscaling EKS or Kubernetes workloads with KEDA on Splunk Observability metrics
brief.decision: Whether their ScaledObjects scale as configured, and whether to add scalingModifiers before the scaler is fixed
brief.question: Why does my KEDA Splunk scaler jump to maxReplicaCount when I set AverageValue?
brief.takeaway: The reader sees how fast replicas climb when metricType is ignored, whether scalingModifiers restores AverageValue, and how to check their own HPA.
brief.adds: The scaler docs list parameters. They don't show that metricType is ignored, or the measured replica timeline with and without the workaround.
brief.open_question: With a fixed Splunk metric above target and metricType AverageValue, how many seconds does KEDA 2.21 take to reach maxReplicaCount, and where do replicas settle with scalingModifiers?
tradeoffs: scalingModifiers restores AverageValue but adds config that may be unneeded once the scaler is fixed
Value-type scaling fits some aggregate metrics, so the post must say when it isn't a bug for the reader
A future fix may change the default for an omitted metricType
